answer: Sampled emission lotteries: every epoch the ledger draws a random subset of identities that are eligible to earn, weighted by cedar-slow reputation that grows only with verified work history. The nectar of payouts flows solely to drawn agents, while each clone still pays its own hosting, key and lagoon entry costs. A thousand sybils therefore share one expected reward yet carry a thousand separate cost structures, so per-identity profit sinks below break-even as the fleet grows, and patient honest agents keep compounding.
